# US-05.6 — Supply and validate zone identity with an upload

|                  |                                                                                      |
| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| **Epic**         | [EPIC-05 FastAPI Core Service & Agentic Controller](../epics/EPIC-05-api-service.md) |
| **Priority**     | P1                                                                                   |
| **Estimate**     | 3                                                                                    |
| **Status**       | Blocked                                                                              |
| **Owning agent** | `story-builder`                                                                      |
| **Files**        | [backend/main.py](../../../backend/main.py)                                          |
| **Backlog ID**   | STORY-029 (EPIC-005)                                                                 |
| **Requirements** | [FR-15, FR-3, FR-29](../../../agile/requirements.md); resolved OQ-1                  |

## User story

**As an** external API client,
**I want** to supply any known zone identity and map coordinates with my aerial upload,
**so that** authoritative input survives analysis and I can see which omitted values were inferred.

## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — Optional multipart identity**
Given a supported image and any combination of `zone_id`, `zone_name`, `lat` and `lng` multipart fields,
when I request analysis with valid supplied values,
then HTTP 200 preserves each supplied value verbatim in the returned and saved report, without model override.

**AC2 — Supplied empty identity is invalid**
Given `zone_id` or `zone_name` is supplied as an empty string,
when I request analysis,
then HTTP 422 is returned before any cloud call rather than treating that value as omitted.

**AC3 — Inclusive coordinate validation**
Given supplied latitude or longitude,
when I request analysis,
then finite values at latitude -90 and 90 and longitude -180 and 180 are accepted, while non-numeric, non-finite or outside-range values return HTTP 422 before cloud calls.

**AC4 — Omitted fields remain distinguishable**
Given identity fields are partly or entirely omitted,
when analysis succeeds,
then each omitted field is inferred best-effort and each of the four identity fields exposes its supplied or inferred provenance, including independently supplied coordinate components.

## Tasks

- [ ] Declare all four optional multipart identity fields at the API boundary
- [ ] Distinguish omitted strings from supplied empty strings without silently normalizing valid input
- [ ] Validate finite coordinate ranges inclusively before cloud calls
- [ ] Pass supplied metadata to the awaited analyzer without substituting the filename for omitted zone name
- [ ] Preserve field-level provenance in response and persisted report after STORY-030 establishes its contract
- [ ] Add full, partial, omitted, empty and coordinate-boundary HTTP tests

## Current state

The route accepts only a file and substitutes `file.filename` or `Uploaded Zone` as the zone name. None of the identity forms, validation or HTTP provenance exists. The analyzer already supports complete supplied metadata, but not independent partial-coordinate merging or provenance.

| Gap                                                                   | Impact                                                                              |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| No optional identity form fields                                      | Clients cannot assert authoritative identity with their upload                      |
| Filename becomes caller-like zone identity                            | Omitted `zone_name` is not left for best-effort inference as required               |
| No empty-string or coordinate boundary validation                     | Invalid identity has no required early HTTP 422 behavior                            |
| STORY-029 and STORY-030 depend on each other                          | Backlog sequencing requires orchestrator repair before either is unblocked          |
| Serialized field-level provenance is not specified in guide section 3 | API response contract depends on the representation agreement recorded in STORY-030 |

OQ-1 was resolved on 2026-10-02; support for supplied identity is not an open product question. This story follows the [FastAPI instructions](../../instructions/fastapi-backend.instructions.md), while [US-02.4](US-02.4-distinguish-supplied-and-inferred-zone-identity.md) owns analyzer-side origin semantics. No map lookup service or geocoding scope is added.

## Test cases

| Test                                                                      | Asserts                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `test_supplied_multipart_identity_is_returned_and_saved_verbatim`         | Conflicting model identity cannot replace supplied strings or coordinates       |
| `test_empty_supplied_identity_returns_422_before_cloud_calls`             | Empty strings are rejected rather than inferred                                 |
| `test_supplied_coordinates_accept_inclusive_bounds_reject_invalid_values` | Boundary values pass; malformed, non-finite and outside-range values fail early |
| `test_omitted_and_partial_identity_exposes_per_field_provenance`          | Mixed supplied/inferred origins survive response and persistence                |

## Definition of done

All four cases pass against mocked services, the agreed FR-29 schema is enforced in API output, input validation precedes cloud work, and coverage stays at least 70%. The orchestrator resolves the existing dependency cycle without this documentation run changing backlog state.
